items.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012
items.q: So the room was filled with Ray Nance, Clark Terry, Duke Ellington, and I mean Duke, I knew him intimately as I know you basically now.

ctx.x: Yeah. How’s the Communism going? Gee.

But during the time of the war, the Russians at the beginning were our enemies of course, as you remember. Then they came around to our side after Hitler invaded them. And all of a sudden I found myself playing in a Communist meeting one night. You know, and this drummer, who I had no idea was a Communist, he said, “You’ve got to play this gig for these people I’m in this group with.” I said, “yeah?” We go there and there’s a big Russian flag. But anyway I mean the war was — they were on our side, and we had…

we would do is to have a weenie roast or whatever, spaghetti night, and invite them all over. So the room was filled with Ray Nance, Clark Terry, Duke Ellington, and I mean Duke, I knew him intimately as I know you basically now. The last time I saw him I was with Benny at the Rainbow Grill at Rockefeller Center, and I went to the Stage Delicatessen and Harry Carney, the baritone player, was sitting there: “Hey Peter, how are you.” I said, “Harry, how are you?” He said, “What are you doing working here?” I said,…
